Kimberly —

Quick read and my preliminary positions below. Happy to take this offline with Contracts, but flagging what I think we can and should hold for the business: 

1) Per-incident sub-limit (security incidents) — recommend: lesser of $2M or 3x annualized fees for the affected account for catastrophic incidents; a lower fixed per-incident amount for routine (e.g., $500k).
2) Annual aggregate cap — set at 3x ARR or $5M (whichever is lower) across all incidents to avoid open-ended exposure.
3) Exclusions — keep carve-outs for our willful misconduct and gross negligence only; no carve-outs that expand to third-party acts unless tied to control.
4) Remedies — prefer to preserve broad remedies (customers can seek direct damages) but exclude consequential/punitive and speculative loss (loss of business, future profits). Credits as primary immediate remedy remain fine for many customers but shouldn't be the exclusive remedy for high-severity breaches.

Language suggestions to hand to legal: define "Security Incident" narrowly; include a step-up remediation and escalation path; tie sub-limit triggers to incident classification (severity 1/2/3).

I'll mark up the attached and send in-line edits by EOD.

-Rishi
Sr. Counsel, Commercial

Kimberly —

Thanks for the materials and for the clear framing. Brightline's position is: we can accept a sub-limit, but only if the overall MSA cap is sufficient and there is a mutuality principle (i.e., both parties' liability for incidents is pro-rated). We cannot accept language that carves out negligence-related breaches from liability.

Counter-proposal (high level):
- Mutual cap at 3x annual fees for the 12-month period preceding the incident.
- Incident-specific cap: 1.5x monthly recurring fees or $750k (whichever is greater) for incidents resulting from Redwood's operational failure.
- Exclude recovery for incidental/punitive damages (we'd accept direct damages), but we want data restoration and forensics costs to be recoverable outside a pure credit remedy.
- We will not accept a bucketed "willful misconduct only" carve-out that removes liability for gross negligence.

Attaching our redlines for the Order Form — see attached file: brightline-redlines-orderform.docx.

Samira Khan
Contracts & Commercial Operations
Brightline
